The zvstBTC strategy and its zv-* contracts are a separate leveraged product, not an eighth ordinary lending vault.

granite.name: Granite
granite.summary: USDCx lending market; sBTC is collateral; the deprecated aeUSDC market closes 2026-11-03
notes: Use the live USDCx rows: what `state-v1` allows or selects, the contracts those call, and the read-only `utility` below. The market's logic and state span two deployers. SPSX722... holds the entrypoints, governance and their modules. SP3M2BY... holds `state-v1` and shared contracts the live logic still calls, including `meta-governance-v1` (governance membership) and `staking-reward-v1`. Rows labelled historical are older SP3M2BY... logic from the official contracts page. Live contracts do not call them, and `state-v1` rejects the old borrower, liquidity provider, liquidator and staking.

The current flash-loan endpoint still takes its callback trait from the old deployer SP3M2BY.... It lends USDCx only; sBTC collateral support does not make it an sBTC lender. Exact principals: [Granite recipe](../granite.md#granite).
Deprecated: the aeUSDC market closes by 2026-11-03 ([announcement](https://x.com/GraniteBTC/status/2115575726975922272)). Its rows remain only so open positions can exit and reopen in USDCx.
The repository's `.mock-usdc` is a test dependency. Use [deployed asset/callback rules](../granite.md#granite).

The row labelled `historical pyth-adapter-v1 (Pyth Core)` is a legacy Pyth Core adapter. The live borrower and liquidator call SPSX722... `pyth-adapter-v1`, which verifies Pyth Lazer updates; see the [oracle path](../granite.md#granite-oracle-path). Granite's own Lazer instance is under [Pyth Lazer](pyth-lazer.md).

The `utility` row under SPDMQAB... is a read-only USDCx helper, not an entrypoint. Its `get-market-state` returns balances, the asset cap and totals with interest accrued to now; its cap reads are in [withdrawal caps](../granite.md#granite-withdrawal-caps). Other `utility` contracts exist under SPSX722..., SP3M2BY... and other deployers; use the SPDMQAB... row.

Granite also runs staging markets on mainnet with real assets. The staging USDCx market under SP2N615... has its own `state-v1`, entrypoints, governance and `utility`. Older staging plans in the repository name other deployers. Never use staging contracts for production calls.

The pinned repository revision is newer than the production logic: its `borrower-v1`, `liquidator-v1` and `withdrawal-caps-v1` differ from the deployed contracts. Read the deployed source for production behavior.

An increasing version suffix or `pool-created = true` does not prove a usable quote. Recheck tokens, core, active/quotable flags and current liquidity.
The old deployed-address docs lag current API deployments. For ABI/version differences, see [swap guidance](../bitflow.md#bitflow).

alex.summary: Current SDK AMM v2 set; flash loans disabled at sampled tip
notes: The official SDK/app selects the AMM v2 deployment below; older docs list a different historical deployer. Do not combine those sets.
The vault's flash-loan flag is currently false, so ALEX is not a flash-loan source.
The actual ALEX token defines native `alex` and `alex-locked` assets. Verify exact token/trait identity; other ALEX wrappers are separate.

The mainnet docs mix legacy SP3K8... contracts with the current SDK AMM v2 family. Old deployment names do not establish current integration targets; the aggregator also binds specific wrapper contracts.

pyth-lazer.name: Pyth Lazer
pyth-lazer.summary: Protocol-owned verifier instances (Zest v2, Granite); no shared oracle
notes: Each instance belongs to the protocol that deployed it: Zest v2 (`SP1A27...`) and Granite (`SPMV5HDZ...`, the dedicated deployer in Granite's deployment plan). Upstream requires each consumer to deploy and govern its own instance; calling another protocol's instance makes its governance key your price authority ([deploy your own](../../../oracles/SKILL.md#deploy-a-lazer-instance-for-your-protocol)).

Both currently trust the same Pyth signer key, charge no fee and are unpaused. Each is governed by one single-signature key, and its signer changes take effect at once. Recheck signer identity and expiry, decoder, fee and pause state before use.
Use [Lazer units and payload rules](../../../oracles/SKILL.md#lazer-consumer-rules); legacy Pyth Core is not supported for new Stacks integrations.

stacks-swap.name: Zest Protocol Stacks Swap
stacks-swap.summary: On-chain routes across DEXes and Stacking DAO; exact route ABI required
notes: Selected routers/adapters, not an exhaustive deployment list. Match the quote's exact ABI and bound dependencies; a newer suffix does not establish current selection. See [integration rules](../stacks-swap.md#stacks-swap).

velar.name: Velar
velar.summary: Dharma AMM contracts and exact Stacks Swap adapter dependencies
notes: Dharma AMM deployment identities only; supported pools, route selection, fees and liquidity require live checks. Do not confuse these with Artha perpetuals or assume identical ABI.
Its wSTX principal is venue-specific; use the exact wrapper required by the selected route.

dia.name: DIA: USDh/USD oracle
dia.summary: USDh/USD push oracle and trait, separate from Pyth Lazer
notes: This DIA oracle is the only on-chain source of a USDh/USD price: any contract that values USDh reads it here. Zest prices USDh from it; Hermetica, the USDh issuer, does not use it. One updater key pushes the values. Its timestamps are milliseconds (Pyth Lazer uses microseconds), and a missing key reads as a zero value and timestamp rather than an error: check provenance and freshness yourself.
